name: אָדָם
summary: The first man, whom Yahweh God formed of dust from the ground on the sixth day, set in the garden of Eden, and from whose rib he built the woman; husband of Eve, father of Cain, Abel and Seth; he lived 930 years and died (Gen 2–5). His name is the noun אָדָם, “man”, itself: through Gen 2–4 he is “the man” (הָאָדָם), from Gen 4:25 the same word stands without the article as his name, and Gen 5:2 says God “called their name אָדָם in the day they were created”, the name of the kind borne by its first member. The text sets the word beside אֲדָמָה, the ground he was taken from and returned to (Gen 2:7; 3:19). The New Testament names him as the first man, through whom sin and death came to all, and as a type of Christ, “the last Adam” (Rom 5:12–14; 1Co 15:22, 45).

evidence.note: “Male and female he created them, and he blessed them and called their name אָדָם in the day they were created”: scripture’s own account of the name.
“Yahweh God formed הָאָדָם, dust from הָאֲדָמָה”: the man named beside the ground he was formed from.
“Until you return to הָאֲדָמָה, for out of it you were taken.”
Yahweh God brought the beasts and birds “to הָאָדָם to see what he would call them”.
“And to אָדָם he said”: pointed here, and in Gen 2:20; 3:21, without the article.
“אָדָם knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth”: the word without the article, as a name.
“This is the book of the generations of אָדָם. In the day God created אָדָם, in the likeness of God he made him”: the name and the noun in one verse.
Adam lived 130 years and begot Seth “in his likeness, according to his image”; “all the days that אָדָם lived were 930 years, and he died”.
The genealogy begins אָדָם שֵׁת אֱנוֹשׁ.
The genealogy of Jesus ends “τοῦ Ἀδὰμ τοῦ θεοῦ”, of Adam, of God.
“Death reigned from Adam to Moses … Adam, who is a type of the one to come.”
“As in Adam all die, so also in the Christ all shall be made alive.”
Gen 2:7 quoted with both the noun and the name: “ὁ πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος Ἀδὰμ became a living soul; ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδὰμ a life-giving spirit”. The Peshitta writes אָדָם in both places.
“Ἀδὰμ was formed first, then Eve; and Adam was not deceived.”
“ὁ, indecl. (Heb. אָדָם)”: the Greek is the Hebrew name carried over.
The Peshitta New Testament’s ܐܕܡ: Luk 3:38; Rom 5:14; 1Co 15:22, 45; 1Ti 2:13, 14; Jud 14.

note: No bdb key: the name has none of its own, its tokens being inside a.bc.ab, the noun אָדָם, which the root entry claims. TIPNR’s Adam@Gen.2.19 lists both אָדָם and הָאָדָם as his forms, so every הָאָדָם of Gen 2–4 is tagged to him. Where the article can be seen in the consonants (הָאָדָם) the text has “the man”; לְאָדָם in Gen 2:20; 3:17, 21 is pointed without it; Gen 4:25 is the first place the bare word must be the name. Hos 6:7 (כְּאָדָם, “like Adam” or “like men”) and Job 31:33 (כְאָדָם) may name him but either reading fits, so they are not cited. Deu 32:8 בְּנֵי אָדָם is “sons of man”. The town Adam (Adam@Jos.3.16) is a place and has no entry. Arabic آدَمُ is the Hebrew name borrowed (Lane p. 37); Ugaritic and Phoenician ʾdm are the noun “man”, on which the name rests.
